title: An open stub transforms into a shunt short at quarter wave

checks.derivation: An open stub is a short at f=1/(4td), nulling transmission.
At f=1/(2td), the open stub is open again.
At f=1/(8td), normalized shunt admittance is j; S21=2/(2+j).
A lossless shunt short reflects all incident power.

evidence.provenance: First-principles network limits or algebraic reduction of the declared teaching loop, independent of production numerical output.

prediction: Can an open-ended branch suppress transmission on the through path?
explanation: Yes. The impedance seen at the junction depends on electrical length. At quarter wave the open end transforms into a short; at half wave it transforms back to an open.
limitations: Exact-null evaluation is a floating-point approximation to a singular tangent.
No finite-bandwidth impulse reconstruction is inferred.
